verification_scope: Primary pages checked where cited; no independent reproduction, tool installation, network scan or credential retrieval.

items.title: Attention and transformer visual explanations
items.claim: Animations introduce embeddings, attention scores, softmax, context vectors and transformer blocks.
items.assessment: Useful conceptual reference. A few video frames do not establish the full derivation; the post promising a path to ChatGPT in seconds is an illustration, not a training recipe.
items.next: Keep; reproduce a tiny attention calculation before treating the diagrams as a tutorial.

items.title: Recommendation systems
items.claim: An animated simulation illustrates how recommendations learn from viewer choices.
items.assessment: Toy data and displayed accuracy describe the demonstration; they do not explain a specific commercial recommendation system.
items.next: Keep for learning; make a small recommender and measure held-out ranking quality.

items.title: Decision trees and overfitting
items.claim: Weather-like features route through a decision tree; deeper trees memorize training samples.
items.assessment: Good learning prompt. The screenshot percentages are simulation results, not transferable benchmark guarantees.
items.next: Keep; compare depth-limited trees on train and held-out data.

items.title: Google AX orchestration
items.claim: AX declares agent workloads, workspaces and models and supports sandboxed execution.
items.assessment: The official repository confirms the runtime and warns of major breaking changes. Billion-task language is a design ambition, not a benchmark verified here.
items.next: Read architecture only if cluster orchestration is a current bottleneck; park migration.

items.title: STAIR structured retrieval
items.claim: The post says a retriever hallucinates 65 times less and implies zero liability.
items.assessment: The paper defines hallucination here as generating an invalid document identifier. Its 3.25% versus 0.05% figures explain the 65-fold ratio. This is not end-to-end answer accuracy, universal replacement of RAG, or a liability guarantee.
items.next: High-value reading: evaluate structure-aware retrieval on a small representative document set before considering a change.

items.title: SwaT cross-family KV transfer
items.claim: Swarm Telepathy transfers internal cached states between model families; the post cites better accuracy and speed.
items.assessment: The abstract reports mean 40% higher accuracy and fourfold speed in its experiments. This uses learned KV-cache transfer, not communication between arbitrary closed chat APIs. It needs internal model-state access.
items.next: Research watchlist; inspect model/runtime requirements before any reproduction.

items.title: The Trinity capability-driven improvement
items.claim: Creator, Explorer and Evolver roles reorganize task experience into reusable capabilities.
items.assessment: The paper reports 34-point gains on training benchmarks and 26 on unseen benchmarks. These are author-reported results for evolved harnesses; they do not establish unrestricted autonomous self-improvement.
items.next: Read for evaluation and capability-reuse ideas; do not transplant the architecture from a summary.

items.title: AKV cache engineering
items.captured_from: Raymond de Lacaze / LLMs and Agentic AI
items.claim: Agents can drop selected KV entries and adjust retained positions without rewriting the text trajectory.
items.assessment: The abstract describes serving-engine support and reports cost and latency gains. These operations are not simply a shorter prompt and require compatible infrastructure.
items.next: Park implementation unless serving your own models; keep as architecture research.

items.title: JEPA representation alignment
items.claim: The post frames a 109M-parameter model outperforming 72B-parameter models as a broad scaling reversal.
items.assessment: The paper concerns cross-modal representation alignment and good paired views. Its theorem has assumptions. Alignment results do not establish that the small model is a better general assistant.
items.next: Keep the paper; read the task definition and theorem assumptions before reusing the comparison.

items.title: Weight-space programming
items.claim: A frontier LLM directly edits a small fraction of another network’s weights without gradient training.
items.assessment: The author blog reports a targeted Qwen looping fix, with forward-pass feedback. It also reports failure to materially improve a non-looping Gemma model. This is not a general replacement for model training.
items.next: Keep on research watchlist; read limitations alongside the successful case.

items.title: Web scraping through an MCP connector
items.claim: A post connects Ultimate Web Scraper as a custom MCP and asks Claude to collect a catalog.
items.assessment: The connector/service identity, pricing, permissions and actual extraction quality are not established by these frames. The broad headline is not evidence that every site can be scraped.
items.next: Park until a real extraction task exists; verify the exact connector first.

items.title: Voice input: Wispr Flow
items.claim: Sponsored video shows voice-to-text input.
items.assessment: Advertisement captured as a lead; no accuracy, platform support or cost checked.
items.next: Optional trial only if dictation friction is a real problem.

items.title: Agent harness workshops
items.captured_from: Md Ismail Sojal; workshop thumbnails from AI Engineer / beamnxw
items.claim: Posts recommend workshops on separating agent reasoning, tools, state and recovery.
items.assessment: Primary Anthropic writing supports incremental work, persistent progress and environment checks. The exact videos, salary story, 10x reliability and 60% faster-token claims were not verified.
items.next: Read the primary article; extract one recovery/checkpoint idea for a future scoped experiment.

items.title: Browser Use
items.claim: Browser Use lets an AI agent operate a browser.
items.assessment: The repository exists. The social-media follower-export demonstration is not a measured reliability claim. Browser automation still needs task-specific validation.
items.next: Keep for a concrete browser task; compare with existing tools before adding another runtime.

items.title: Agentmemory persistent memory
items.claim: A site advertises memory that types back.
items.assessment: The site identity matches the screenshot. Its operational benefits were not tested; session-memory collection and retention need review before adoption.
items.next: Park unless current memory retrieval has a demonstrated failure.

items.title: Scientific Agent Skills
items.claim: A scientific skills collection packages domain workflows for agents.
items.assessment: The project exists and the former claude-scientific-skills URL redirects to scientific-agent-skills. Existence is not validation of every domain procedure.
items.next: Select one skill for an actual scientific task; review its sources before using it.

items.title: Diagram Design collection
items.claim: A diagram collection shows flowcharts, state machines, ER diagrams and swimlanes.
items.assessment: The title is legible, but the owner/repository URL is not established. Do not install a similarly named project based only on this title.
items.next: Keep the design reference; recover an exact repository link only when needed.

items.title: Community cybersecurity skills
items.claim: A reel presents Anthropic Cybersecurity Skills.
items.assessment: The mukul975 repository explicitly identifies itself as an independent community project, unaffiliated with Anthropic. The title is not vendor endorsement.
items.next: Keep with corrected attribution; review individual skill code and scope before adoption.

items.title: Awesome Harness Engineering
items.claim: A resource collection advertises agent harness patterns and templates.
items.assessment: The title is readable, but the exact repository owner is missing. It is a discovery lead rather than an installation recommendation.
items.next: Park until an exact source is recovered.

items.title: OpenViking context database
items.claim: OpenViking combines context resources for agents.
items.assessment: Official repository identity matches. This is additional infrastructure; its value depends on a concrete memory/retrieval problem and measured benefit.
items.next: Keep as a candidate; do not adopt solely from the feature list.

items.title: HackerTube curation example
items.claim: A post describes Karpathy building a video catalog from Hacker News recommendations.
items.assessment: His own blog confirms the project account and data-export option. A personal success story is not a general two-hour delivery estimate.
items.next: Useful inspiration for this clipping inbox: source selection, topic grouping and portable export.

items.title: Backend learning map
items.claim: A reel lists servers, APIs, databases, caching, queues, containers and observability.
items.assessment: A useful topic checklist, not an ordered curriculum or proof that ten pieces make a complete backend.
items.next: Use as a gap checklist for one small project.

items.title: Ten programming repositories
items.claim: The list includes build-your-own-x, awesome, public-apis, freeCodeCamp, free-programming-books, system-design-primer, developer-roadmap, coding-interview-university, awesome-python and project-based-learning.
items.assessment: These are discovery/catalog resources with different purposes. Repository identities are transcribed from frames; individual current contents and recommendations were not audited.
items.next: Pick one path or project; avoid treating all ten as a study backlog.

items.title: GitHub URL shortcuts
items.claim: A reel shows the dot-key web editor shortcut, GitMCP and Gitingest.
items.assessment: GitHub docs confirm github.dev and GitMCP documents the domain conversion. Gitingest was visible, but its website timed out during this check.
items.next: Keep as convenience references; verify service boundaries before sharing non-public code.

items.title: Developer roadmaps
items.claim: A reel points to interactive developer roadmaps.
items.assessment: roadmap.sh offers community roadmaps. A roadmap is a selection aid, not a requirement to learn everything.
items.next: Choose only the next missing skill for the project in hand.

items.title: Bolt browser builder
items.claim: A video shows a Bolt new-project interface.
items.assessment: The screenshot identifies a product lead; it does not establish cost, generated-code quality or deployability.
items.next: Park unless comparing application scaffolding tools.

items.title: Transform.tools
items.claim: A converter transforms data/code representations such as SVG to JSX.
items.assessment: The site exposes those conversion categories. Output still needs review against the target application.
items.next: Keep as a reference for non-sensitive conversions.

items.title: Algorithms overview
items.claim: A poster names binary search, sorting, Dijkstra, dynamic programming and BFS.
items.assessment: Useful retrieval cue. Complexity annotations need their assumptions and do not substitute for understanding the algorithm.
items.next: Keep; implement only the algorithm relevant to a current task.

items.title: HTTP/REST versus WebSocket
items.claim: A visual contrasts request-response calls with a persistent bidirectional connection.
items.assessment: A useful first approximation. The poster does not cover HTTP connection reuse, HTTP/2, HTTP/3 or server-sent events.
items.next: Keep as an introductory explanation; choose a protocol from actual interaction requirements.

items.title: Serving a million users: pagination
items.claim: An interview question asks how an API should return records from a million-row users table.
items.assessment: Cursor pagination and indexes are plausible directions. Actual design also depends on filtering, ordering, authorization, payload size and consistency. Ignore the destructive joke in the comments.
items.next: Practice explaining a bounded page size, stable cursor and matching index; measure query behavior on test data.

items.title: FIFO versus LRU cache eviction
items.claim: An animation compares hit rates for two eviction policies under the same illustrated traffic.
items.assessment: The percentages apply to that workload. LRU does not universally dominate FIFO; admission policy, workload and memory overhead matter.
items.next: Keep; use a replay of real request traces before selecting a cache policy.

items.title: API versus endpoint
items.claim: A visual distinguishes a single operation/address from the set of API operations and rules.
items.assessment: Useful beginner framing. An endpoint should be understood with its HTTP method, contract and authentication, not just its URL.
items.next: Keep as a teaching reference.

items.title: DevOps concepts
items.claim: A poster summarizes twelve DevOps concepts.
items.assessment: A vocabulary map, not evidence that the listed stack is required for every project.
items.next: Use as a discussion checklist; defer tools without an operational need.

items.title: ast-grep
items.claim: A reel recommends ast-grep among underrated repositories.
items.assessment: The upstream repository confirms structural code search and rewriting. The screenshot itself contains little usage detail.
items.next: Potentially useful: test a read-only structural search on a small fixture before any rewrite.

items.title: Forward Deployed Engineer portfolio
items.claim: A post proposes twelve enterprise projects spanning tenant isolation, SSO, connectors, RAG, webhooks, deployment, redaction, incidents, billing, onboarding and a case study.
items.assessment: Good requirements prompts. It does not establish hiring requirements or the need to build twelve separate systems.
items.next: Prefer one integrated project: tenant-scoped webhook intake, idempotency, retries, metrics and a short case study.

items.title: Cybersecurity job advertisement
items.claim: A Czech advertisement offers an on-site cybersecurity role at Solvertech.
items.assessment: Keep separately from technical advice. Availability and compensation were not checked and can expire.
items.next: Only revisit if job searching; verify on the employer site.

items.title: SaaS moat discussion
items.claim: A community post asks what SaaS survives AI competition; a reply mentions a moat beyond code.
items.assessment: A strategic question, not evidence for a business prediction. Useful only when grounded in customers, distribution, data or switching costs.
items.next: Park as a prompt for a real product decision.

items.title: Linux security starter stack
items.claim: A LinuxTeck sequence covers Lynis, UFW, Fail2ban, Nmap, tcpdump, OpenVAS, Suricata, Wazuh, AppArmor/SELinux and password hashing.
items.assessment: Lynis is confirmed upstream as an audit tool. The rest is a useful captured overview, not an audited deployment recipe. Empty/transition frames and set-and-forget wording omit important configuration and monitoring context.
items.next: Start with a disposable Linux VM and a documented baseline; select layers from actual exposure.

items.title: Blue-team monitoring lab
items.claim: A reel combines OSSEC, Suricata and Zeek in a lab.
items.assessment: Keep the detection/visibility idea. Screenshots of terminals do not validate the depicted detections, performance or integration.
items.next: Design one local benign test event and require evidence at collection, detection and alert stages.

items.title: Zero Trust concepts
items.claim: A poster covers per-request verification, identity, least privilege, device health and segmentation.
items.assessment: Use as a vocabulary card. A slogan or product does not demonstrate these controls actually hold.
items.next: Map three ideas to one application and identify evidence that each control works.

items.title: Security fundamentals
items.claim: A poster lists threat modeling, input validation, rate limiting, encryption, hashing, secret handling, logs and patching.
items.assessment: Good interview/review prompts; a static list cannot establish security coverage.
items.next: Keep; connect each chosen concept to a concrete failure and test.

items.title: Wireshark investigation filters
items.claim: Frames show filters for long DNS names, TXT records, curl user agents, SYN traffic and a service-name string.
items.assessment: Wireshark documents the DNS fields. These filters select observations; none alone proves tunneling, exfiltration or compromise. Retain a baseline and packet context.
items.next: Use a benign saved lab capture to explain why each matching packet is or is not suspicious.

items.title: Advanced networking fragment
items.claim: An intro, reflected-attack sketch and OSI-layer graphic appear in a networking reel.
items.assessment: There is too little of the explanation to reconstruct a reliable technique or lesson.
items.next: Park as an incomplete reference; recover the original video only if needed.

items.title: Beginner hacking guide fragment
items.claim: A reel labeled Beginner Hacking Guide is Trap shows a terminal.
items.assessment: The single frame is insufficient to recover an actionable lesson or source.
items.next: Park; do not turn it into a command recipe.

items.title: WAF identification: WAFW00F
items.claim: A reel names WAFW00F as a tool for identifying web application firewalls.
items.assessment: Tool-name reference only; this frame does not verify the target, result or tool version.
items.next: Keep only if a permitted web-testing task needs this information.

items.title: AI-assisted pentesting frameworks
items.claim: Station X presents PentestGPT, XBOW, Nuclei AI, HexStrike AI, NodeZero and building your own wrapper.
items.assessment: PentestGPT has an upstream project. Nuclei really supports -ai, with a ProjectDiscovery API key and cloud interaction; it is not proof of a separate Nuclei-ai product. Other benchmarks and command examples were not audited.
items.next: Keep for comparison on an intentionally vulnerable local lab; no framework installed or scan run.

items.title: Commercial automated security platforms
items.claim: A reel names NodeZero, Pentera, XBOW and Equixly; one frame is blank/transition.
items.assessment: Names are identifiable but capabilities, independence of testing, access requirements and pricing were not checked.
items.next: Park until a defined assessment need and evaluation criteria exist.

items.title: Unclear AI hacking-tool list
items.claim: A reel appears to name PoisonGPT, WormGPT, an OpenPentest-like agent, NeuroSploit-like text, a Free...GPT name and Nebula.
items.assessment: Several names are obscured or ambiguous. Exact spelling, legitimate upstream owners and advertised capabilities are unresolved. Do not substitute guessed download links.
items.next: Low priority; recover the original source before considering any item.

items.title: OSINT and public search services
items.claim: Hunter.io, PublicWWW, ZoomEye and GitHub are visible in an ethical-hacking search-engine list.
items.assessment: Two frames are too dark to identify confidently. Group the readable services by what they search; they are not interchangeable or evidence of permission to access a result.
items.next: Keep readable names as leads; recover missing names only for a real research question.

items.title: Reverse engineering tools
items.claim: Station X shows GhidraMCP, Frida and ImHex.
items.assessment: ImHex has a matching upstream repository. A GhidraMCP label can refer to different integrations; this reel does not establish the exact owner. Frida usage and integration details remain unchecked here.
items.next: Keep ImHex as a concrete lead; identify the exact MCP project before any installation.

items.title: Password and Wi-Fi audit toolbox
items.claim: Frames name Aircrack-ng, CrackStation, Hashcat, John the Ripper and Hydra.
items.assessment: Aircrack-ng upstream confirms a Wi-Fi assessment suite. These tools serve different tasks; transitions and repeated frames do not form a tutorial or benchmark.
items.next: Reference only; choose a single learning exercise on owned test data if a need arises.

items.title: Games and prompt-injection practice
items.claim: Station X lists Uplink, Hacker Simulator, Hacknet, Grey Hack, ThreatGEN, TIS-100, EXAPUNKS, Bitburner, Bandit and SecureBot.
items.assessment: Bandit is confirmed by its operator as beginner training. Entertainment games, programming puzzles and real command-line exercises have different learning goals; the reel does not validate transfer to operational security.
items.next: Start with a short Bandit session if shell fundamentals need practice. Keep games as optional recreation.

items.title: Hypit video variation workflow
items.claim: Hypit advertises generating variants of video workflows, including face and scene swaps.
items.assessment: The upstream repository matches. View-count promises and the 45-video visual are marketing claims, not performance evidence.
items.next: Park unless there is a concrete video task using material you have permission to reuse.

items.title: Text-to-CAD
items.claim: The repository describes AI-assisted physical-product design.
items.assessment: The exact upstream owner is earthtojake. Generated CAD still needs dimensional and manufacturing validation; stars do not establish fit for a specific part.
items.next: Optional experiment: a simple noncritical bracket with explicit dimensions and an inspected export.

items.title: Geo-sleuth photo-location skill
items.claim: A skill combines maps, elevation, imagery and street view to infer photo location.
items.assessment: The Oldcircle repository matches. The demonstration precision is not a general accuracy guarantee. No personal/travel photo was submitted or geolocated in this review.
items.next: Optional test on a public landmark image with known ground truth; record errors and evidence.

items.title: Fibonacci clock visual
items.claim: A clock illustration uses a Fibonacci spiral.
items.assessment: Interesting visual-design reference, with no demonstrated programmer or security workflow benefit.
items.next: Keep as low-priority inspiration.

items.title: Windows network reset tip
items.claim: A video shows netsh int ip reset in an administrator terminal.
items.assessment: A context-free troubleshooting command is not a diagnosis. Do not run it just because a saved reel recommends it.
items.next: Park; revisit only with a specific Windows networking fault.

items.title: Saved Wi-Fi password Python snippet
items.claim: A Python snippet wraps Windows netsh commands to display saved profiles and keys.
items.assessment: This describes local credential retrieval, not cracking arbitrary Wi-Fi. Text parsing and shell invocation are fragile. No code was run or credentials retrieved.
items.next: Low priority; retain only as a conceptual reference.

items.title: IPChat room-based messaging
items.claim: A reel shows ipchat.in with a room-based messaging interface.
items.assessment: A landing-page frame does not establish privacy, encryption or service trustworthiness.
items.next: Park; no sensitive material or account access supplied.

items.title: TCP/TLS animated fragments
items.claim: Two frames refer to three messages, TLS, AES-GCM and ChaCha20.
items.assessment: Potential introductory network explanation. There is insufficient context to infer protocol-version details or a complete handshake.
items.next: Keep with incomplete label; recover a full explanation before using it as teaching material.

items.title: CA key incident fragment
items.claim: A graphic shows a CA private-key value of four and hints at a company incident.
items.assessment: No incident identity or primary source is recoverable from this frame. It cannot substantiate a claim about a real CA.
items.next: Park until the incident and source can be identified.

items.title: Hosting after AI-assisted app generation
items.captured_from: Claude Ai Community / IndigoSea1295 and comments
items.claim: A community post asks where people host mobile apps made with Claude; comments mention Lovable, Railway, Vercel, Cloudflare, Netlify and Supabase.
items.assessment: Comments mix web hosting, backend services and development tools. They do not establish a native mobile release workflow or which service fits a particular app.
items.next: Keep as a requirements prompt: identify web versus native client, backend and data needs before choosing hosting.
